scenario: AITA for leaving to see my GF when my sister told me not to when she was "in charge"? | My mom is gone for a class thing in another state, and my dad is on a business trip so its just me, my sister and my brother all alone in the house. My sister is 18, I am 17 and my brother is 12, I don't know why but my parents still felt the need to leave my sister "in charge" while they were both gone. My sister lets the power go to her head and while she can generally make my little brother obey her she has a tougher time with me. On Sunday I was gonna go out with my GF for dinner, and my sister stopped me saying that I can't leave. When asked its cause "she said so", I laughed at that and I thought she was joking but she just kept looking and I knew it was a joke. I told her she can boss (little brother's name) around but she can't boss me, and I went out with my GF. I guess my younger brother heard all the commotion and called mom saying we were "fighting" and when I came home and my mom called me she said that I'm grounded and have to dow what my sister says cause she's "in charge". I protested as best as I could but she wasn't having it and grounded me for disobeying my sister who is a pseudo parent while they are away. I just dropped it cause its not worth arguing any point with my mom. AITA here? EDIT:My brother told me afterwards that he was the one that told mom, I forgave him cause I mean I can't be mad at that little turd for too long

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing in this situation. Let me start by understanding the scenario. My parents are away, and my sister, who's 18, is supposed to be in charge. I'm 17, and my brother is 12. My sister tends to take her role too seriously, especially with me. On Sunday, I wanted to go out with my girlfriend for dinner, but my sister told me I couldn't. She said, "I said so," which I thought was a joke at first. I laughed, but she wasn't kidding. I told her she can boss my little brother around but not me, and I went out anyway. When I came home, my brother had called our mom and said we were fighting. My mom called me and grounded me, making me do whatever my sister says because she's "in charge." I tried to protest, but my mom wasn't having it. I ended up dropping it because arguing wasn't worth it. My brother later told me he was the one who called mom, and I forgave him because he's just a kid. So, the question is: Did I do the right thing? Is it AITA (Ask if I'm the Asshole)? First, I need to consider the dynamics here. My sister is 18, and I'm 17. My parents left her in charge, which is a big responsibility. She's trying to enforce rules, but she's struggling with me. I went out with my girlfriend despite her objections. My sister isn't a parent, but my mom is treating her as such when she's away. I think about why I went out. I felt that my sister wasn't the authority figure, and I didn't have to listen to her. But my mom grounded me for not obeying her, which made me feel like I was being punished for standing up for myself. On the other hand, my sister is trying to do her job, and my mom is backing her up. Maybe I should have respected her authority more, even if I didn't agree with it. But I also feel that I'm almost an adult myself, and my sister isn't really equipped to make decisions for me. I also consider the impact on my brother. He's 12, and he might have been scared or confused when he heard the commotion. He told our mom, which led to the grounding. I forgave him, but it's still part of the situation. I wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I could have talked to my sister instead of just going out. Or maybe I could have explained why I wanted to go out. But I was 17, and I felt like I should be able to make that decision. Another angle is the role of my parents. They left my sister in charge, but maybe they didn't set clear expectations for both of us. My sister might have overstepped, and I might have understepped by not respecting her authority. I also think about the consequences. I was grounded, which was a punishment for disobeying. But I also feel like I was right in asserting my independence. It's a tricky balance between respecting authority and asserting one's own autonomy. In the end, I'm not sure if I was the asshole or not. I did what I thought was right, but it led to negative consequences. Maybe I should have handled it differently, like discussing it with my sister instead of just going out. But I also feel like I was within my rights to make that decision.
